analyst_view.overall: Early view: a straight fight for a play-off place between 23rd and 24th, both on 4 points. Christian Ilzer's Hoffenheim went into the break ninth in the Bundesliga after beating Schalke 2-1, but Ozan Kabak is suspended and several defenders (Albian Hajdari, Robin Hranac among them) were injured in early November; Sturm are fourth in Austria but lost 3-2 at home to Celje last time.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.0 goals. Hoffenheim's stretched back line could help a Sturm side that has scored only three times in four European games, and Hoffenheim's home games ended 2-3 and 3-0, so I stay close to the number.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.5 corners, most of them for Hoffenheim. Ilzer's side should have long spells of pressure at home, so a double-figure count fits.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.0 cards. I lean a little higher: both sides badly need the points, Hoffenheim's back line will be patched up without Kabak, and Alexander Prass's red card at Leverkusen this autumn shows they can lose their heads. The referee has not been named.

shots.text: The numbers say 31.3 shots, which is high. Hoffenheim at home, with Andrej Kramaric and Prass in form and Fisnik Asllani and Tim Lemperle scoring against Schalke, should produce plenty, and Sturm will need to come out more than usual.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.9 shots on target. Sturm's Oumar Diakite scored twice against Celje, so they can hurt a weakened defence, while Hoffenheim should create the bulk; I stay with the number.
